name: RNO-G
summary: A staged in-ice radio observatory near Summit Station extends ultra-high-energy neutrino searches into the Northern Hemisphere.
physics_targets: Astrophysical and cosmogenic neutrinos above about 10 PeV
detection_principle: Deep and shallow antennas detect Askaryan radio pulses from showers in Greenland ice. A low-threshold phased trigger, surface veto and complementary antenna polarisations improve event identification and reconstruction.

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: Eight stations were operational in the August 2026 DESY account, with continued construction toward 35.

timeline.event: First stations deployed and science data taking began.
Eight deployed stations reported; beamforming trigger operation described.
DESY described eight operating stations and plans to add four.

key_parameters.value: Eight stations operational in the DESY August 2026 report; further additions were prospective

results.summary: Construction, commissioning and radio-background studies demonstrate operating stations; no UHE-neutrino discovery is claimed by these sources.
